solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rogue Republican replaced by quiet man of science

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and another put in its place, as a player is replaced by a substitute

blocks.note: a rogue is a rascal
R is the abbreviation for Republican
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A disgraced politician makes way for a hushed scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the R from RASCAL and put P in its place to get PASCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise Pascal was a French mathematician and physicist, an example of a scientist.

clue.text: Unreasonable to pay songwriter thus?

blocks.note: first meaning: contrary and wrong-headed
second meaning, read cryptically: paying a lyricist at a rate for each stanza

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical definition: a lyricist paid PER VERSE; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means stubbornly contrary or illogical, a synonym for unreasonable.

clue.text: The right way out for England manager?

blocks.note: first meaning: an exit on the south side, the right-hand side when facing east
second meaning: Gareth, who managed the England football team from 2016 to 2024

explanation.walkthrough: Facing east, south lies to your right, so a south gate is a way out on the right. Gareth Southgate managed England's men's football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Southgate is literally a gate to the south and the surname of a former England football manager.

clue.text: A Muslim boy? You're having me on!

blocks.note: first meaning: ..., a common Muslim given name
second meaning: the scoffing retort used when you disbelieve something

explanation.walkthrough: Run together, the boy's name Asif is the exclamation 'As if!'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As if!' is a sarcastic expression of disbelief, and Asif is an Arabic boy's name.

clue.text: Perfectionist's criticism about left back

indicators.note: going back means these letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to give someone stick is to criticise them
re means about or concerning
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A football fussbudget criticises the left back for every slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' reads like a football position, but 'back' turns round RE and L together. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact correctness in every detail, a synonym for a perfectionist.

clue.text: Victorian novelist, woman of dubious virtue, I hear

indicators.note: I hear signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

blocks.note: a trollop is a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: Gossip about a nineteenth-century author's scandalous female character.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote the Barsetshire novels in the Victorian era.

clue.text: European court case abandoned for a period

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal case at a European court dropped for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' looks like dropping the case but signals the letters running wild.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretaceous is a geological period, the last of the dinosaur age.

clue.text: Let lecturer facilitate

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lecturer
to ease is to make easier

explanation.surface: Allow the teacher to make things easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' reads as 'allow'; it means rent out.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease a property is to rent it out, the same as to let it.

clue.text: Tell queen to cheer up

blocks.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
to elate is to make very happy

explanation.surface: Instructing the monarch to brighten up.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it, a synonym.

clue.text: Maybe Tarzan appears among them angrily

indicators.note: appearing among them means sitting inside the run of words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of 'them' and start of 'angrily'

explanation.surface: The jungle king shows up in a rage among a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan is an example of a muscular macho man, which 'maybe' flags.

clue.text: Defeat in Europe ultimately? Typical!

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
taken as written
the last letter of Europe

explanation.surface: A sigh at yet another national loss on the European stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means ordinary or standard, a synonym for typical.

clue.text: General on top of everything

blocks.note: over means on top of
all means everything

explanation.surface: A military general who keeps on top of every detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military officer but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall as an adjective means taking everything into account, a synonym for general.

clue.text: Reminder of the code word for an E

blocks.note: first meaning: something that recalls or resembles an earlier thing
second meaning: the word used for that letter in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hint about the secret word that stands for a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a faint repetition that calls something back to mind, and Echo is the radio alphabet's word for E.

clue.text: Liberal MP, I learnt, receiving answer in house

indicators.note: receiving means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other
liberal means free and loose, so the letters may be rearranged freely

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat MP recounts what they learnt on getting an answer in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal MP' looks like a politician, but 'Liberal' is the anagram signal for the letters of MP I LEARNT plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a legislative chamber, as in the House of Commons, so parliament fits.

clue.text: Follower embracing fashionable field of study

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a disciple is a follower
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A devotee taking up a trendy academic subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follower embracing' reads like a fan hugging something, but the follower is the outer word wrapped round the fashionable one.
explanation.definitionFit: A discipline is a branch of learning, a direct synonym for a field of study.

clue.text: Still delighted to have left City

indicators.note: having left means it has gone away, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: ecstatic means overjoyed
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A fan still thrilled that a player has walked out on the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like a football club; it is the City, London's financial district, whose postcode EC comes off the front of ECSTATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means not moving, a synonym for still as an adjective.

clue.text: Placate monkey, feeding it some greens?

indicators.note: food goes inside an animal, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: an ape is a monkey loosely
peas are green vegetables

explanation.surface: Calming an angry monkey by offering it vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that peas are only one kind of greens, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to calm them by giving them what they want, a synonym for placate.

clue.text: Dante odes somehow completely lifeless

indicators.note: somehow means in an unspecified manner, so the letters come out in an unknown order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic finds the Italian poet's verses utterly dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-dead means dead beyond doubt, an intensified form of lifeless.

clue.text: Foresight of puritan overseeing northern church

blocks.note: a prude is a puritanical person
N is the abbreviation for northern
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The wisdom of a strict Puritan presiding over a church in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'overseeing' just means placed above, so the puritan comes first and the rest sits below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is careful forethought about future risk, a synonym for foresight.

clue.text: Obsessed by British being in poor shape

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
eaten up means consumed by a feeling

explanation.surface: A Briton so fixated that their health suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' places B beside the phrase for obsessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten-up describes something battered and worn, a synonym for in poor shape.

clue.text: What might have poisoned Freddie?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about how some man called Freddie was poisoned
setter's reading: Freddie is the Queen singer whose surname is also a toxic liquid metal

explanation.walkthrough: The surname of Freddie, the Queen frontman, is also a toxic metal; the clue reads like a murder mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: The liquid metal element is a notorious poison and also the surname of the rock singer Freddie.

clue.text: Hide money in Sweden, causing an outcry

blocks.note: an animal's hide or pelt
the öre is a Swedish coin, a hundredth of a krona

explanation.surface: A scandal over money stashed in a Swedish account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb about concealment; it is a noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public anger or excitement, a synonym for outcry.

clue.text: Stress Bill has little money

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Bill is worried because he is short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the emphasis placed on a syllable, a synonym for stress.

clue.text: Argues tearfully, clutching hotel resident

indicators.note: clutching means holding tightly within, so the letters sit inside the words before

blocks.note: spans the end of 'Argues' and start of 'tearfully'

explanation.surface: Someone tearfully rows while holding on to a hotel visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a person staying at a hotel, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Exhausted, having located pup running amok

indicators.note: running amok means rampaging out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Worn out after finally finding a puppy that had been running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapped-out is British informal for worn out, usually of a car or machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out describes something worn out and broken down, a colloquial synonym for exhausted.

clue.text: Loves visiting a paper abroad

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
the Financial Times, this very paper
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Romantic affairs carried on while reading a newspaper overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' looks like overseas but means current or astir, as in 'rumours are abroad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means in circulation or under way, matching abroad in its sense of widely current.

clue.text: Tendency to be dishonest

blocks.note: first meaning: a natural inclination or aptitude
second meaning: British slang for corrupt, as of a crooked police officer

explanation.surface: A note on someone's leaning towards crooked behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination, and bent is also slang for corrupt or crooked.

clue.text: Hotshot failing to finish march

indicators.note: failing to finish means the word stops short of its last letter

blocks.note: a demon is someone brilliant at something

explanation.surface: A star athlete fails to complete the march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like a verb or month; it is a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for a demonstration, a protest march.

clue.text: Anger perhaps as best-selling book withdrawn

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a best-seller is number one, No 1, with the digit as I
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Outrage after a chart-topping book is pulled from shops.
explanation.walkthrough: NO I and TOME together, read backwards, give EMOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is one example of a strong feeling, which the 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Has that woman visited Soweto drinking den?

blocks.note: she refers to that woman
with 'has', has been means has visited

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman has called at a bar in a Johannesburg township.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Has that woman visited' as SHE has BEEN. Soweto is a township near Johannesburg, where shebeens are common.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking house, especially in South Africa and Ireland.

clue.text: Carried half-sister inside and nearly fell

indicators.note: half means only part of the word, here its back portion, is kept
inside means one piece sits within another

blocks.note: to tote is to carry
the second half of sister

explanation.surface: Someone carried their half-sister and almost stumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-sister' looks like a relative; it is half the word sister, placed inside TOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily and almost topple, so tottered fits nearly fell.

clue.text: Auditor's gone into hiding, resulting in delay

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a listener, so what follows is judged by its sound

blocks.note: holed up means hiding away

explanation.surface: An accountant goes missing, holding up the audit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant; it means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is a delay, as in traffic, a direct synonym.
